title: Nigerian Navy at 70: Tinubu Commissions 3 Warships, Launches Gulf of Guinea Maritime Task Force
detail: President Bola Tinubu presided over the Nigerian Navy's 70th anniversary International Fleet Review in Lagos on June 1, commissioning three new warships — NNS Oloibiri, NNS Mambila, and NNS Gurara — and inaugurating a Combined Maritime Task Force for the Gulf of Guinea. The multilateral maritime initiative brings together Côte d'Ivoire, The Gambia, Ghana, Liberia, and Sierra Leone to combat piracy, crude oil theft, and illegal fishing across West African waters. Tinubu praised the Navy for eradicating piracy from Nigerian territorial waters, noting that the Gulf of Guinea had been removed from the high-risk zone list maintained by global maritime insurers. The Fleet Review marked a significant milestone in Nigeria's bid to project maritime dominance in West Africa.

media.caption: Tinubu commissions three warships and launches Gulf of Guinea maritime task force at Navy's 70th anniversary

title: Central Bank of Nigeria Reshuffles All Four Deputy Governors
detail: Effective June 1, 2026, the Central Bank of Nigeria redeployed all four Deputy Governors to new portfolio assignments as part of a major management restructuring. Dr. Muhammad Sani Abdullahi was reassigned to Corporate Services, Philip Ikeazor to Economic Policy, Emem Usoro to Operations, and Lamido Yuguda to Financial System Stability. The reshuffle comes as the CBN presses ahead with banking sector recapitalisation — requiring Nigerian banks to raise Tier 1 capital before December 2026 — and its ongoing inflation-management and exchange rate stabilisation reforms. Analysts viewed the reshuffle as part of Governor Olayemi Cardoso's effort to align CBN departmental leadership with the bank's reform priorities.

media.caption: CBN reshuffles all four Deputy Governors as banking recapitalisation and reform programme accelerates
